subject: maths
title: Percentages
seo_title: Year 5 Percentages Worksheets: 100% as the Whole, Fractions and Decimals
standard_text: Recognise that 100% represents the complete whole and use percentages to describe, represent and compare relative size; connect familiar percentages to their decimal and fraction equivalents
meta_desc: Free Year 5 percentages worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: per cent as parts of 100, 100% as the whole, 50%, 25%, 10% and 1% as fractions and decimals, comparing sizes and real-life problems. 100 maths questions with an answer key, great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Per cent means out of 100, and 100% is the whole: 37% = 37/100 = 0.37.
key_sub: Know 50% = 1/2 = 0.5, 25% = 1/4 = 0.25, 10% = 1/10 = 0.1 and 1% = 1/100 = 0.01. To compare, change everything into percentages: 0.5 = 50% > 45%.
body_html:
Per cent means out of 100

Per cent (%) means out of 100. Split a whole into 100 equal parts. Each part is 1%.

100% is the whole

All 100 parts make the whole, so 100% = 1 whole. The parts always add up to 100%.

100% means all of something, not 100 things. If a class of 25 students all go on an excursion, 100% of the class is 25 students.

Percentages to know

To change a fraction into a percentage, make the denominator 100.

PercentageFractionDecimal
50%120.5
25%140.25
75%340.75
20%150.2
10%1100.1
1%11000.01
Example

Write 15 as a percentage.

5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 too: 15 = 20100.

Answer: 20%

Comparing

Change every number into a percentage, then compare.

Example

Order 0.4, 45% and 310 from smallest to greatest.

0.4 = 40%, 45% and 310 = 30%.

Answer: 310, 0.4, 45%

Test score

Isla scores 18 out of 20. What percentage is that?

20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the score by 5 too: 1820 = 90100.

Answer: 90%

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.4 = 4%0.4 = 0.40 = 40%
15 = 15%15 = 20100 = 20%
45% > 0.5 because 45 > 50.5 = 50%, so 45% < 0.5
100% means 100 things100% means the whole, however many there are

faq.q: What do Year 5 students learn about percentages in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 5 (AC9M5N04) students learn that 100% is the complete whole, use percentages to describe and compare amounts, and connect familiar percentages such as 50%, 25%, 10% and 1% to their fractions and decimals.

faq.q: How do you explain percentages to a Year 5 child?
faq.a: Show a hundred square: the whole is 100 small squares, and each square is 1%. If 37 squares are shaded, 37% is shaded, which is also 37/100 or 0.37.

faq.q: Which percentage, fraction and decimal facts should Year 5 know?
How do you compare a percentage, a fraction and a decimal?
faq.a: Change them all into percentages first. For 0.4, 45% and 3/10, write 40%, 45% and 30%, so the order from smallest is 3/10, 0.4, 45%. This kind of question also appears in NAPLAN numeracy.

items.q: What does per cent mean?
items.e: “Per cent” means out of 100. 23% means 23 parts out of 100 equal parts.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 37 of the 100 squares are shaded, so it is 37%. 63% is the white part.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 6 full columns of 10 are shaded: 60 of the 100 squares = 60%. 6% would be only 6 small squares.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 8 of the 100 squares are shaded: 8%. 80% would be 8 full columns.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: Only 1 of the 100 squares is shaded: 1%. 10% would be a full column.

items.q: 1% of a hundred square is how many small squares?
items.e: The square has 100 small squares. 1% = 1 out of 100 = 1 small square.

items.q: Which hundred square shows 30% shaded?
items.e: 30% = 30 out of 100 = 3 full columns of 10. That is B. A shows only 3%, C shows 70% and D shows 33%.

items.q: A box has 100 tiles. 13 of them are blue. What percentage of the tiles are blue?
items.e: 13 out of 100 = 13100 = 13%. 87% are not blue.

items.q: In a survey of 100 students, 64 like footy. What percentage like footy?
items.e: 64 out of 100 = 64100 = 64%. 36% is the students who do not.

items.q: Write 23% as a fraction.
items.e: Per cent means out of 100: 23% = 23100.

items.q: Write 9% as a fraction.
items.e: 9% = 9 out of 100 = 9100. 910 would be 90%.

items.q: Write 71100 as a percentage.
items.e: 71100 means 71 out of 100, so it is 71%.

items.q: Write 6100 as a percentage.
items.e: 6100 = 6 out of 100 = 6%. 60% would be 60100.

items.q: Write 45% as a decimal.
items.e: 45% = 45100 = 45 hundredths = 0.45.

items.q: Write 7% as a decimal.
items.e: 7% = 7100 = 7 hundredths. Hundredths are the second place after the point: 0.07. 0.7 is 70%.

items.q: Write 0.29 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.29 = 29 hundredths = 29100 = 29%.

items.q: Which decimal is the same as 99%?
items.e: 99% = 99100 = 99 hundredths = 0.99. It is just less than 1 whole.

items.q: Which shows the shaded part in three ways?
items.e: 25 of 100 squares: 25100 = 25 hundredths = 0.25 = 25%.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is not shaded?
items.e: 52 squares are shaded, so 100 − 52 = 48 squares are white: 48%. 58% is a common slip: check 52 + 58 = 110, not 100.

items.q: Mia has shaded 70 squares. How many more squares must she shade to show 75%?
items.e: 75% = 75 squares. 75 − 70 = 5 more squares. 30 is the number of white squares, not the squares to add.

items.q: 100% of something means …
items.e: 100% = 100100 = 1 whole. So 100% is the whole amount, however many things there are.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: All 100 squares are shaded: 100 out of 100 = 100%. 100% is the whole.

items.q: Write 100% as a decimal.
items.e: 100% = 100100 = 1 whole. 0.01 is only 1%.

items.q: Which is not the same as the whole?
items.e: The whole is 100% = 100100 = 1. 10% is only one tenth of the whole.
4 × 25% = 100%. Four quarters make the whole.
80% + 20% = 100%. Count on from 80 by tens: 90, 100. That is 2 tens = 20.

items.q: What percentage of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The whole bar is 100%, split into 10 equal parts. Each part is 10%. 7 parts = 70%.
35% + 65% = 100%. Count on from 35 to 100: 5 to 40, then 60 to 100. So 65%. 75% is a common slip: 35 + 75 = 110.

items.q: What percentage of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The whole bar is 100%, split into 4 equal parts. Each part is 100% ÷ 4 = 25%. 14 = 25%, not 14%.
42 + 58 = 100, so the missing part is 58%. Check: 42 + 68 = 110, not 100.

items.q: What percentage of the bar is shaded?
items.e: 100% ÷ 5 = 20% for each part. 2 parts = 20% + 20% = 40%. 60% is the white part.
7 + 93 = 100, so the missing part is 93%. 3% only makes 10%.

items.q: Which pair makes 100%?
45% is green and 30% is blue. What percentage is white?
items.e: Green and blue: 45% + 30% = 75%. The whole is 100%, so white is 100% − 75% = 25%. 75% is the shaded part.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is not shaded?
items.e: Shaded: 36 + 24 = 60 squares. Not shaded: 100 − 60 = 40 squares = 40%.

items.q: A class has 25 students. 100% of the class go on the school excursion. How many students go?
items.e: 100% means the whole class, all 25 students. 100% does not mean 100 people.

items.q: Liam has read 100% of his 60-page book. How many pages has he read?
items.e: 100% is the whole book: all 60 pages. 100% does not always mean 100 things.

items.q: Ruby has coloured 65% of her poster. What percentage is still to be coloured?
items.e: The whole poster is 100%. 100% − 65% = 35%. Check: 65 + 35 = 100.

items.q: A cake is cut into 10 equal pieces. 4 pieces are eaten. What percentage of the cake is left?
items.e: The whole cake is 100%. Each piece is 100% ÷ 10 = 10%. 6 pieces are left: 60%. 40% was eaten.

items.q: Ava, Leo and Mei share a garden bed. Ava has 50%, Leo has 30% and Mei has the rest. What percentage does Mei have?
items.e: Ava and Leo: 50% + 30% = 80%. The whole bed is 100%, so Mei has 100% − 80% = 20%.

items.q: Write 12 as a percentage.
items.e: 12 = 50100 = 50%. Half of 100 is 50. Do not just write the digits 1 and 2.

items.q: Write 0.5 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.5 = 5 tenths = 50 hundredths = 50%. 5% would be 0.05.

items.q: Write 14 as a percentage.
items.e: 4 × 25 = 100, so 14 = 25100 = 25%.

items.q: Write 0.25 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.25 = 25 hundredths = 25%.

items.q: Write 110 as a percentage.
items.e: 10 × 10 = 100, so 110 = 10100 = 10%.

items.q: Write 75% as a decimal.
items.e: 75% = 75100 = 0.75.

items.q: Write 34 as a percentage.
items.e: 14 = 25%, so 34 = 3 × 25% = 75%. 25% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 15 as a percentage.
items.e: 5 × 20 = 100, so 15 = 20100 = 20%. 15% just writes the digits 1 and 5.

items.q: Write 0.4 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 40 hundredths = 40%. 4% would be 0.04.

items.q: Write 1% as a decimal.
items.e: 1% = 1100 = 1 hundredth = 0.01. 0.1 is 10%.

items.q: Write 1100 as a percentage.
items.e: 1100 means 1 out of 100 = 1%.

items.q: Write 20% as a decimal.
items.e: 20% = 20100 = 210 = 0.2. 0.02 is only 2%.

items.q: Write 310 as a percentage.
items.e: 310 = 30100 = 30%. 3% would be 3100.

items.q: Write 25% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 25% = 25100. 4 × 25 = 100, so it is 14.

items.q: Write 10% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 10% = 10100 = 110. 1100 is 1%.

items.q: Write 20% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 20% = 20100. 5 × 20 = 100, so it is 15.

items.q: Which is not equal to 50%?
items.e: 50% = 50100 = 12 = 0.5. 0.05 is only 5%.

items.q: Which is correct?
items.e: 34 = 75100 = 0.75 = 75%. So 34 = 0.75 = 75% is correct.

items.q: What is 50% of 40?
items.e: 50% = 12. Half of 40 is 20. 10 is 25% of 40.

items.q: What is 10% of 50?
items.e: 10% = 110. 50 ÷ 10 = 5. 40 is what is left after taking away 10, not 10%.

items.q: Which is greater: 0.5 or 45%?
items.e: 0.5 = 50%. 50% > 45%, so 0.5 is greater. Do not compare 5 and 45.

items.q: Compare 0.7 and 7%.
Which is greater: 0.4 or 45%?
Which is greater: 14 or 0.25?
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 0.25. They are equal.

items.q: Which is greater: 0.07 or 10%?
Which is greater: 310 or 25%?
items.e: 310 = 30%. 30% > 25%, so 310 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 0.6 or 58%?
Which is greater: 15 or 15%?
items.e: 15 = 20%. 20% > 15%, so 15 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 34 or 0.8?
items.e: 34 = 0.75. 0.8 = 0.80. 0.80 > 0.75, so 0.8 is greater.

items.q: Which is less than 10%?
items.e: 0.08 = 8 hundredths = 8%. 8% < 10%, so 0.08. 0.8 = 80%, 15 = 20% and 0.12 = 12%.

items.q: Which is greater than 12?
items.e: 12 = 50%. Only 55% is more. 0.45 = 45%, 25 = 40% and 0.05 = 5%.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all as percentages: 0.4 = 40%, 310 = 30%, 14 = 25%. The greatest is 45%.

items.q: Which is the smallest?
items.e: As percentages: 0.5 = 50%, 48%, 14 = 25%, 0.3 = 30%. The smallest is 14.

items.q: Which is between 25% and 50%?
items.e: 0.3 = 30%, which is between 25% and 50%: 0.3. 0.03 = 3%, 0.6 = 60% and 15 = 20%.

items.q: Which is closest to 50%?
items.e: 0.48 = 48%, only 2% away from 50%. 0.4 = 40%, 0.05 = 5% and 34 = 75%. So 0.48.

items.q: Harper says, “45% is greater than 0.5, because 45 is greater than 5.” Is she right?
items.e: Change them to the same kind of number: 0.5 = 50 hundredths = 50%. 45% < 50%. So no, because 0.5 = 50%.

items.q:
How many of these are greater than 50%?
0.6, 25, 55%, 0.45
items.e: As percentages: 60%, 25 = 40%, 55%, 45%. Only 60% and 55% are greater, so 2.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
0.4, 45%, 310
items.e: As percentages: 0.4 = 40%, 45%, 310 = 30%. Smallest first: 310, 0.4, 45%.

items.q:
Order from greatest to smallest:
12, 0.45, 60%, 15
c: 12, 15, 60%, 0.45
60%, 12, 0.45, 15
0.45, 60%, 12, 15
60%, 0.45, 12, 15
items.e: As percentages: 12 = 50%, 0.45 = 45%, 60%, 15 = 20%. Greatest first: 60%, 12, 0.45, 15.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
9%, 0.2, 110, 15%
items.e: As percentages: 9%, 0.2 = 20%, 110 = 10%, 15%. Smallest first: 9%, 110, 15%, 0.2.

items.q: Which sign means half price?
items.e: Half = 12 = 50%. So 50% off takes off half the price.

items.q: This bar shows how much of a game has downloaded. What percentage has downloaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 10%. 3 parts = 30%. 70% is still to download.

items.q: Cooper’s tablet battery has 4 equal bars. 3 bars are green. What percentage is charged?
items.e: 3 of 4 bars = 34. 14 = 25%, so 34 = 75%. 25% is the empty part.

items.q: Ava’s phone shows 40% battery left. What percentage of the charge has been used?
items.e: A full charge is 100%. 100% − 40% = 60% has been used.

items.q: The marks split the rainwater tank into 4 equal parts. What percentage of the tank is full?
items.e: The water is up to the first of 4 equal parts: 14 = 25%. 75% is the empty part.

items.q: A netball team won 60% of its games this season. What percentage of its games did it not win?
items.e: All the games are 100%. 100% − 60% = 40%.

items.q: Lachlan gets 7 out of 10 in a times tables quiz. What percentage is that?
items.e: 710 = 70100 = 70%. 30% is the part he got wrong.

items.q: A bus for the athletics carnival is 100% full. There are 48 students on it. How many seats are there?
items.e: 100% full means every seat is taken. So there are 48 seats. 100% does not mean 100 seats.

items.q: A rainwater tank is 25% full. What fraction of the tank is empty?
items.e: 25% is full, so 100% − 25% = 75% is empty. 75% = 34.

items.q: Shop A has 25% off. Shop B has 15 off. Which shop takes off more?
items.e: 15 = 20%. 25% > 20%, so Shop A takes off more.

items.q: In a quiz, Sienna gets 45% of the questions right. Charlotte gets 0.5 of the questions right. Who gets more right?
items.e: 0.5 = 50%. 50% > 45%, so Charlotte gets more right.

items.q: A 2 L bottle of water is 50% full. How much water is in it?
items.e: 50% = 12. Half of 2 L is 1 L. 2 L would be 100%.

items.q: Mei scores 18 out of 20 in a spelling test. What percentage is that?
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the score by 5 too: 1820 = 90100 = 90%. 2 is the number of marks she missed.

items.q: At the school sausage sizzle, 50% of the 60 sausages have been sold. How many have been sold?
items.e: 50% = 12. Half of 60 is 30. 10 is 60 − 50.

items.q: A T-shirt costs $40. A sign says 50% off. How much do you pay now?
items.e: 50% off means half the price is taken off. Half of $40 is $20, so you pay $40 − $20 = $20. $30 takes off only $10.

items.q: Jack’s water bottle is 0.6 full. Kai’s is 65% full. Both bottles are the same size. Whose bottle has more water?
items.e: 0.6 = 60%. 65% > 60%, so Kai’s bottle has more water.

items.q: In a class survey, 34 of the students like cricket and 70% like swimming. Which is liked by more students?
items.e: 34 = 75%. 75% > 70%, so cricket is liked by more students.

items.q: William scores 16 out of 20 in a maths test. What percentage is that?
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 1620 = 80100 = 80%. 4 is the number of marks he missed.

items.q: In Chloe’s garden, 0.3 of the flowers are red, 45% are yellow and the rest are white. What percentage are white?
items.e: 0.3 = 30%. Red and yellow: 30% + 45% = 75%. White: 100% − 75% = 25%. 52% comes from reading 0.3 as 3%.

items.q: A film is 50% downloaded after 10 minutes. At the same speed, how long will it take to download 100%?
items.e: 50% is half. Half took 10 minutes, so the whole takes 10 + 10 = 20 minutes.
